We ask how people divide work with a language model, handing a task over or working through it, and whether industry returns track that delegation. The data are the Anthropic Economic Index releases from {{< var design.release.r1 >}} to {{< var design.release.r6 >}}: conversations matched to O\*NET tasks, aggregated to occupations, countries and {{< var design.n_industries >}} Fama–French industries. The protocol is pre-registered ({{< var pap.tag >}}). H1, less delegation in high-education and high-wage occupations, is {{< var rq1.h1.decision_text >}}. H2, delegation rising within tasks across releases, is {{< var rq1.h2.decision_text >}}: its measured rise is one step between releases coinciding with a change of the classified-conversation base. H3, more checking where errors are costly, is {{< var rq1.h3.decision_text >}}. H4, country differences in delegation conditional on task mix, is {{< var rq1.h4.decision_text >}}. Across industries, delegation and human-rated theoretical exposure have a Spearman correlation of {{< var rq2.b.z_delegation.z_eloundou.rho >}} [{{< var rq2.b.z_delegation.z_eloundou.ci.lo >}}, {{< var rq2.b.z_delegation.z_eloundou.ci.hi >}}], partly through shared occupational weights and zero-assigned unpublished occupations. The market test's minimum detectable effect, {{< var d11.primary_mde >}} pp of annualised alpha per SD of exposure, exceeds the plausibility threshold of {{< var design.plausibility_pp >}} pp, so under rule D11 the market evidence is reported as what it can and cannot yet say: H5 is {{< var rq3.h5.decision_text >}} and H5b is {{< var rq3.h5b.decision_text >}}. The employment weights postdate formation, so RQ2, H5 and H5b are out of sample in AEI data only. Robustness rows change no decision; @sec-robustness names those moving each estimate most.
